## Introduction

This post demonstrates how R and Python can be used together in a single Quarto document. R is used to calculate the mean body mass of each penguin species. The resulting R object is then passed to Python, where it is used for an additional calculation.

The data come from the [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/) dataset from Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

## R: Calculate Mean Body Mass

First, R loads the Palmer Penguins data and calculates the mean body mass for each species.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(reticulate)

penguin_summary <- penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    mean_body_mass_g = mean(body_mass_g),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

penguin_summary
```

The object `penguin_summary` was created in R. It contains one row for each penguin species and its mean body mass.

## Python: Receive the R Object

The following Python chunk accesses the object created in R through `r.penguin_summary`.

```{python}
penguin_summary_python = r.penguin_summary

penguin_summary_python
```

Python is therefore using the result produced by R rather than loading the original dataset and repeating the analysis.

## Python: Use the Transferred Object

Next, Python uses the transferred object to determine which species has the highest mean body mass.

```{python}
heaviest_species = penguin_summary_python.loc[
    penguin_summary_python["mean_body_mass_g"].idxmax()
]

heaviest_species
```

The result identifies the penguin species with the highest average body mass based on the summary originally calculated in R.

## Conclusion

This post demonstrates how R and Python can work together in one Quarto document. R loaded and summarized the Palmer Penguins data and created the `penguin_summary` object. Python then received that R object and used it for an additional calculation.

This demonstrates that an object computed in one language can be passed to and used by another language within the same reproducible Quarto document.
